extracted.intended_audience: U.S. PCT applicants, patent attorneys, and IP practitioners considering MOIP (KIPO/MOIP) as an International Searching Authority / International Preliminary Examining Authority
extracted.subtask_description: Information and evaluative criteria for choosing the Ministry of Intellectual Property (MOIP / KIPO) as an International Searching Authority (ISA) and International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA) for PCT filings, with emphasis on capabilities, timeliness, cost, and support for U.S. applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability as an ISA and IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: MOIP has been available as an International Searching Authority (ISA) and International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA) since 2006 for PCT applications in which the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) is the Receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being an IP5 member and available since 2006 makes MOIP a long-standing option for U.S. PCT applicants seeking ISA/IPEA services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination staff qualifications and credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: MOIP has roughly 900 PCT examiners (MOIP employees who meet requirements such as having a Ph.D., a patent attorney certification, or passing the civil service examination) and about 200 PCT searching personnel (cooperative search company employees who have more than a bachelor’s degree). Expertise in natural sciences and/or engineering is required for all PCT examiners and search staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOIP emphasizes hiring qualified examiners and provides continuous education (specialized lectures and seminars). Statistics provided: Ph.D. holders (44%), state exam passers (16%), patent attorneys (4%), professional engineers (2%); about 950 patent examiners in total. Continuous employment intended to reduce FA pendency and advance quality of exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff technical expertise (domain knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff are skilled in relevant technology fields; about 50% of staff have doctorate degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High share of advanced degrees signals domain expertise across technical areas relevant to patent searching and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language skills and translation capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT examiners and searching personnel possess high levels of language skills necessary to comprehend foreign PCT documents and prepare ISR/IPERs. In-house language programs are available in English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, German, French, and Russian; examiners may also take foreign language courses offered by universities commissioned by MOIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOIP has equipped its search system (KOMPASS) with machine translation software: Japanese-Korean, English-Korean and Chinese-Korean translations of foreign patent documents are available. MOIP states it is able to search and analyze Korean, Japanese and Chinese patent documents as well as those of the US and Europe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search resources, systems and non-patent literature access
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPOnet (internet-based e-filing and work processing platform) and KIPOnet III support filing and examination processes. A specialized PCT outsourcing platform (separate server) and the Patent Search System enable full-text searches of patent gazettes from Korea, Japan, the U.S. and Europe and link to the National Digital Science Library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOIP uses ‘non-patent literature unified meta searches’ for electronic journals (including IEEE, ScienceDirect and OSA) to search multiple Internet sites and show results on the same screen. Additional resources listed include STN, CA, KIPO-BLAST, Thomson Innovation, IEEE, ACM, Springer, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage and historical patent archives
rubrics_metrics.description: MOIP has a database of patent and utility model abstracts in Korean dating back to 1947; full text of granted patents and utility models dating back to 1979; Korean patent and utility model applications dating back to 1983. For international patent data, MOIP collected about 55 different kinds of patent/utility model/design data from 22 countries dating back to 1974.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources providing data include WIPO, USPTO, EPO, and JPO. Coverage lists show various formats and date ranges for Europe, WIPO, U.S., Taiwan, UK, China, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational structure and dedicated PCT divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examination Bureau has been reorganized into specialized bureaus: Patent Examination Policy Bureau, Convergence Technology Bureau, Electricity & Communications Bureau, Chemistry & Biotechnology Bureau, Machinery & Metals Bureau to handle convergence technologies and develop examination policy. There are 35 Examination divisions including 2 exclusive divisions for PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational specialization is presented as a means to efficiently handle technical convergence and to provide focused PCT examination capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination quality assurance and internal review
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination review is mainly conducted by the Examination Quality Assurance Division, directly supervised by the deputy commissioner; it has 12 reviewers for patents, utility models, and the PCT, and 4 reviewers for trademarks and designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dedicated QA division and designated reviewers are cited as mechanisms to ensure quality international searches and consistent examination standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness in transmitting International Search Reports (ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA must establish the ISR within three months from its receipt of the application (the “search copy”), or nine months from the priority date (or, if no priority is claimed, from the international filing date), whichever expires later. MOIP reports it always tries to deliver ISRs in the promised time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOIP performance data for 2020: transmitted 87.5% of ISRs to the IB within three months from date of receipt of the search copy; comparative figures: EPO 76.4%, USPTO 68.9%. Timeliness is calculated as the time elapsed between the priority date and the date on which the ISA transmits the ISR to the IB (or, if applicable, date of receipt of Article 17(2)(a) declaration). Timely ISR delivery is emphasized as crucial for applicants to prepare next stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive international search fees
rubrics_metrics.description: MOIP provides international search services with costs approximately 50% lower than those of other major authorities (except ROSPATENT, ILPO and JPO). A comparative table lists Search Fee (USD) / Preliminary examination Fee for MOIP (1,036 USD / KRW 450,000), EPO (2,091 EUR / 1,830 EUR), USPTO (2,180 USD / 640 USD), JPO (1,476 USD / JPY 58,000 in English), IP Australia (1,697 AUD / 590 AUD), ILPO (1,107 ILS / 1,535 ILS), ROSPATENT (543 RUB / 16,000 in English), IPOS (1,646 SGD / 830 SGD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page presents low cost combined with claimed high quality as a selling point favored by U.S. PCT applicants; fee figures are sourced to WIPO PCT Fee Tables as of 1 July 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost reduction for Korean national phase (demand fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: MOIP provides reduced rates for demand fees for the examination in the Korean national phase. If you submit ISR and/or IPER from MOIP, you will get a 70% reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting MOIP ISR/IPER yields substantial national-phase cost savings when entering the Korean national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant support and help-desk availability for U.S. applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT Korea Help-desk operates in Vienna, VA to provide direct free services for U.S. PCT applicants who designate MOIP as their ISA and/or IPEA, assisting as a contact point and substitute for MOIP in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details and hours are provided (pctkorea@pctkorea.com; 703-388-1066 Mon-Fri 9:00 AM - 18:00 PM ET), offering prompt assistance and various IP information on demand.
